# CI and staging deployment

`CI and staging / verify` runs on pull requests and main in an isolated GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner. It installs the frozen lockfile, builds shared packages, checks types and unit tests, builds all three images, tests real MQTT TLS/ACLs, starts disposable PostgreSQL/Redis/MQTT/S3/API/worker/web containers, migrates and bootstraps twice, and runs real HTTP and Chromium E2E. All five application roles log in; API authorization, school isolation, durable telemetry, duplicate ingestion before and after an API restart (including aggregate counts), persisted CSV reports, and desktop/mobile UI are checked. No test connects to staging. The stack and its database are removed even on failure. Only test logs and screenshots are uploaded, not account fixtures.

Only successful main runs in `nateekarni/solar-roof` publish the **same tested image IDs** to GHCR as commit-SHA tags. The deployed references include registry SHA256 digests; tags are for discovery only. The web image uses the same-origin proxy, with no staging URL baked into the browser bundle. GitHub checkout does not persist credentials. The GHCR token is supplied only to the publication step. Pull requests cannot access staging environment secrets or run deployment.

## One-time setup

1. Protect `main`: require pull requests and successful `verify`; disallow force pushes. `main` is staging. Do not configure `pull_request_target` execution of PR code.
2. Create a GitHub environment named `staging`, restrict deployment branches to `main`. No human approval is required for ordinary successful main runs.
3. Set repository variable `STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` to `false` while configuring the first deployment. This keeps CI/publication working before Coolify exists. Once setup is complete set it to `true`; run the workflow on main once to deploy, then subsequent successful main pushes deploy automatically.
4. Create a Coolify **Git-backed Docker Compose application**, repository `nateekarni/solar-roof`, branch `main`, compose path `/infra/docker/docker-compose.staging.yml`. Configure the required secrets/settings documented beside that compose file. Configure GHCR registry pull credentials on its destination server (a read-packages credential for private images).
5. **Disable Coolify Auto Deploy on push and preview deployments before enabling CI deployment.** Remove old unauthenticated/manual deployment webhooks. GitHub Actions is the only deployment writer; do not run manual deployments concurrently. The helper also explicitly disables push and preview deployment every run.
6. In the GitHub `staging` environment configure variables `COOLIFY_URL` (HTTPS origin, no `/api/v1` suffix), `COOLIFY_APPLICATION_UUID`, `STAGING_WEB_URL` (public HTTPS origin, normally `https://solar.fowir.com`). Add secret `COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` with Coolify application read/write and deployment permissions restricted to the staging team/resource where supported. Never put this token in repository files, URLs, or frontend variables. Restrict API access to the runner/network policy suitable for your Coolify installation.
7. Configure storage secrets before the first deploy. After migration and storage initialization succeed, create the initial administrator from the API service terminal with `pnpm --filter @solar/api db:bootstrap`, supplying `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` securely as described in the staging runbook. Reruns never reset its password; no demo seed data is loaded.

## Deployment contract and failure recovery

Before mutation, CI rejects stale commits that no longer equal main. The helper verifies the application's UUID, repository, main branch, compose build pack and staging compose path; it rejects an already active deployment. The helper PATCHes the application's tested `git_commit_sha`, disables raw push deployment, updates `API_IMAGE`, `WORKER_IMAGE`, `WEB_IMAGE` via the authenticated bulk environment API, then POSTs `/deploy`. It polls the returned matching deployment UUID, rejects failed/cancelled deployments, and verifies the final commit equals the tested SHA. Finally CI probes web login and web health. The private API readiness check runs inside the Coolify stack; no public API port is needed. It never prints API response bodies/tokens, follows redirects with credentials, or retries deployment-triggering POSTs.

Both workflow and staging deployment concurrency have `cancel-in-progress: false`: a new push cannot kill a migration. A timeout does not cancel the Coolify deployment. Inspect Coolify and wait for the active deployment to stop before retrying. Failed readiness leaves the job red; it is not a successful release. Database rollback is never automated. For application rollback use a previously tested commit and its three digest references after checking schema compatibility; back up before migrations that cannot be reversed. Keep deployment access limited to this workflow to prevent mutable configuration races.

Verified API references: [application update](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/applications/update-application-by-uuid), [bulk environment update](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/applications/update-envs-by-application-uuid), [deploy](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/deployments/deploy-by-tag-or-uuid), [deployment status](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/deployments/get-deployment-by-uuid). These are application endpoints; `docker_compose_raw` is not part of the documented application PATCH schema, so this workflow deploys the compose file from the pinned commit.

Local equivalents: `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs`, build `solar-api:ci`, `solar-worker:ci`, `solar-web:ci`, then `bash infra/docker/mosquitto/smoke.sh` and `bash scripts/ci/integration.sh`. They require Docker, pnpm, and Playwright Chromium. CI accounts and passwords are deliberately limited to the disposable `solar_readiness` database and localhost ports.
